chunks: Verily those who are in the presence of your Lord are never too proud to worship and celebrate His praises, and bow in homage to Him.

key_terms.يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ: They arrogate pride / are too proud

ai.seo_question: Who are the beings that never arrogantly refuse to worship God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as referring to the angels, but also extended to the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams, who exemplify perfect humility before God despite their elevated status. The phrase 'do not arrogate themselves' (la yastakbiruna) contrasts with human pride, highlighting that true nobility lies in continuous servitude (ubudiyyah) and glorification (tasbih). This underscores the theological principle that proximity to God is measured by submission rather than rank.
